```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(metafor)
library(meta)
library(dmetar)
library(gtsummary)
library(flextable)
library(patchwork)

df <- readxl::read_excel("Data/Original/df.xlsx") |>
  mutate(
    Author_year = paste0(
      `First Author`,
      ", ",
      `Publication Year`,
      " ",
      ifelse(is.na(`Дубли`), "", `Дубли`)
    ),
    Стома = replace_values(
      Стома,
      "смешанная" ~ "ileo + colo",
      "илео" ~ "ileo",
      "коло" ~ "colo"
    ),
    Дизайн = factor(
      replace_values(
        Дизайн,
        "РКИ" ~ "RCT",
        "ПК" ~ "Prospective cohort",
        "РК" ~ "Retrospective cohort"
      ),
      levels = c("Retrospective cohort", "Prospective cohort", "RCT")
    ),
    Когорта = replace_values(
      Когорта,
      "Общая" ~ "Part of study",
      "Стома" ~ "Full study"
    )
  ) |>
  rename(
    Stomy = Стома,
    Design = Дизайн,
    `Localisation of data` = Когорта,
    `N sample` = `Общая когорта`,
    Male = Мужчины,
    Age = Возраст,
    BMI = ИМТ,
    LOS = Койки,
    `NACh(R)Th` = НАХЛТ,
    Complications = Осложнения,
    `Severe complications` = Тяжелые,
    `Anastomotic leak` = Несостоятельность,
    Infection = Инфекции,
    Mortality = Смерть
  )

tab_tbl <- function(tbl) {
  as_flex_table(tbl) |>
    theme_box() |>
    autofit() |>
    fit_to_width(8) |>
    font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |>
    fontsize(size = 12, part = "all")
}

tab_ME <- function(ME) {
  flextable(ME) |>
    theme_box() |>
    autofit() |>
    fit_to_width(8) |>
    font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |>
    fontsize(size = 12, part = "all")
}

theme_public <- function() {
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
    theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95"))
}

theme_set(theme_public())
```

# Statistical Analysis

Risk of bias in randomized trials was assessed with the Cochrane RoB 2 tool across five domains (randomization process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, outcome measurement and selection of the reported result), with each domain and the overall judgement rated as low risk, some concerns or high risk \[Sterne et al., 2019\]. Non-randomized studies were assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies, which awards up to 4 stars for selection, 2 for comparability and 3 for outcome \[Wells et al., n.d.\]; a study was rated as good quality if it scored at least 3 stars for selection, at least 1 for comparability and at least 2 for outcome, and as poor quality otherwise. The assessments were presented graphically and were not used to exclude studies or to weight the analyses.\
Study characteristics and outcome rates were first summarized descriptively. Continuous variables are reported as mean (SD), median \[Q1, Q3\] and range; categorical variables as counts and percentages.\
For each outcome (anastomotic leak, overall or severe postoperative complications, mortality), event counts and sample sizes were analyzed using a generalized linear mixed-effects model (GLMM) with a binomial likelihood, logit link, and random study-level intercept \[Schwarzer, Carpenter, and Rücker, 2015\].\
A random-effects model was used throughout, with $\tau^2$ estimated by maximum likelihood \[Viechtbauer, 2005\]. Confidence intervals of the GLMM estimates were based on the t-distribution with k − 1 degrees of freedom, analogous to the Knapp-Hartung adjustment \[Knapp and Hartung, 2003\]; the Knapp-Hartung adjustment itself was used in the inverse-variance models. Heterogeneity was reported as the Wald-type Cochran's $Q$ of the GLMM, $I^2$ (derived from this $Q$, with 95% CI) and $\tau^2$ \[Higgins and Thompson, 2002\], together with a 95% prediction interval for each pooled estimate, calculated with the Higgins-Thompson-Spiegelhalter method \[Higgins, Thompson, and Spiegelhalter, 2009\].\
For the anastomotic leak outcome, prespecified subgroup analyses were run by stoma type (ileostomy vs. combined ileostomy/colostomy; colostomy alone included only two studies and was not analyzed separately), study design (retrospective cohort, prospective cohort, RCT) and publication period (\<2010, 2010-2019, ≥2020). Each subgroup was pooled with the same random-effects GLMM, $\tau^2$ was estimated separately per subgroup, and differences between subgroups were assessed using a $Q$-test for subgroup differences \[Borenstein and Higgins, 2013\].\
Stoma-related early complications were analyzed in an exploratory analysis with the same random-effects GLMM, as the proportion of patients with stoma-related complications among all patients with a stoma and among patients with postoperative complications. The numbers of studies reporting each type of stoma-related complication and the numbers of events in each study were tabulated descriptively, without pooling (Tables 3 and 4).\
Small-study effects were assessed for the primary outcome (anastomotic leak, 67 studies), since tests for funnel-plot asymmetry are recommended only when at least 10 studies are available \[Sterne et al., 2011\]. They were assessed visually using funnel plots (on the logit and arcsine scales) and formally using Peters' regression test \[Peters et al., 2006\], supplemented by a meta-regression of the logit proportion on log~10~ sample size \[Viechtbauer, 2010\]. As sensitivity analyses, the GLMM estimate was compared with a conventional inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis of logit-transformed proportions ($\tau^2$ estimated by maximum likelihood, Knapp-Hartung adjustment) and with the Duval and Tweedie trim-and-fill method \[Duval and Tweedie, 2000\]. As trim-and-fill cannot be applied to the GLMM directly, it was applied to the logit-transformed study estimates, and the pooled effect after imputing studies that would restore funnel-plot symmetry was re-estimated with an inverse-variance random-effects model ($\tau^2$ estimated by maximum likelihood); given the substantial heterogeneity, these results were interpreted cautiously.\
Pooled logit estimates and their confidence and prediction intervals were back-transformed to proportions and are reported as percentages. A two-sided p-value \< 0.05 was considered statistically significant. No adjustment for multiple comparisons was made; the results of subgroup analyses and of the small-study tests were therefore interpreted descriptively.\
All analyses were performed in R version 4.6.1 using Positron version 2026.10.1. Meta-analyses were fitted with the **meta** \[Balduzzi, Rücker, and Schwarzer, 2019\], **metafor** \[Viechtbauer, 2010\] and **dmetar** \[Harrer et al., 2021\] packages, risk-of-bias plots were produced with **robvis** \[McGuinness and Higgins, 2021\], and data handling and tables with **tidyverse** \[Wickham et al., 2019\], **readxl**, **gtsummary** \[Sjoberg et al., 2021\] and **flextable**. Package versions are listed in the session information at the end of the document.

# Results

## Bias

Figure 1. Risk of bias summary (RoB 2).
```{r}
#| label: 1-rob-summary
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: "70%"

df_bias <- readxl::read_excel(
  "Data/Original/Полные тексты bias.xlsx",
  sheet = "Итог"
)

library(robvis)
library(tidyverse)

df_RoB <- df_bias |>
  filter(Форма == "RoB 2") |>
  select(Study, D1_randomization:D5_selection, Overall)

bias_plot_1 <- rob_summary(
  data = df_RoB,
  tool = "ROB2",
  overall = TRUE,
  weighted = F
)

bias_plot_1
```

Figure 2. Risk of bias traffic light plot (RoB 2).
``` {r}
#| label: 2-rob-traffic-light
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 8
#| out-width: "50%"

bias_plot_2 <- rob_traffic_light(
  data = df_RoB,
  tool = "ROB2",
  psize = 20
)

bias_plot_2
```

Figure 3. Risk of bias assessment of non-randomized studies (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale).
``` {r}
#| label: 3-nos-plot
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 30
#| out-width: "40%"

df_NOS <- df_bias |>
  filter(Форма == "NOQAF") |>
  arrange(`Publication Year`) |>
  select(Study, Selection:Overall)

bias_plot_3 <- df_NOS |>
  pivot_longer(Selection:Total) |>
  mutate(
    name = factor(
      name,
      levels = c("Selection", "Comparability", "Outcome", "Total")
    ),
    size = factor(ifelse(
      name == "Selection",
      replace_values(value, c(0, 1) ~ 1, 2 ~ 2, c(3, 4) ~ 3),
      ifelse(
        name == "Comparability",
        replace_values(value, 0 ~ 1, c(1, 2) ~ 2),
        ifelse(
          name == "Outcome",
          replace_values(value, c(0, 1) ~ 1, 2 ~ 2, 3 ~ 3),
          replace_values(
            value,
            c(0, 1, 2, 3) ~ 1,
            c(4, 5, 6) ~ 2,
            c(7, 8, 9) ~ 3
          )
        )
      )
    ))
  ) |>
  #head(n = 40) |>
  mutate(Study = factor(Study, levels = unique(Study))) |>
  ggplot(aes(name, fct_rev(Study))) +
  geom_line(aes(group = Study, color = Overall), show.legend = F) +
  geom_point(aes(size = size, fill = Overall), color = "black", shape = 21) +
  geom_text(aes(label = value), size = 7, color = "black", fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(aes(label = value), size = 6, color = "white") +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(7, 9, 11), guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#02C100", "#BF0000"), name = "Risk level") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#02C100", "#BF0000"), name = "Risk level") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Study")

bias_plot_3
```

## Main

Table 1. Characteristics of studies.
```{r}
#| label: 4-characteristics

df |>
  select(
    `Publication Year`,
    Design,
    Stomy,
    `Localisation of data`:`NACh(R)Th`,
    N,
    Complications:Mortality
  ) |>
  mutate(
    `Publication Year` = factor(
      ifelse(
        `Publication Year` < 2010,
        "<2010",
        ifelse(`Publication Year` >= 2020, "≥2020", "2010-2019")
      ),
      levels = c("<2010", "2010-2019", "≥2020")
    ),
    Male = Male / `N sample` * 100,
    `NACh(R)Th` = `NACh(R)Th` / `N sample` * 100,
    Complications = Complications / N * 100,
    `Severe complications` = `Severe complications` / N * 100,
    `Anastomotic leak` = `Anastomotic leak` / N * 100,
    Infection = Infection / N * 100,
    Mortality = Mortality / N * 100
  ) |>
  tbl_summary(
    digits = list(
      all_continuous() ~ c(1, 1),
      all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1),
      `Publication Year` ~ c(0, 0)
    ),
    label = list(
      Design = "Design of study",
      `Localisation of data` = "Data availability",
      `N sample` = "Size sample of study",
      N = "Cohort size",
      Male = "Male rate",
      `NACh(R)Th` = "NACh(R)Th rate",
      Complications = "Complications rate",
      `Severe complications` = "Severe complications rate",
      `Anastomotic leak` = "Anastomotic leak rate",
      Infection = "Infection rate",
      Mortality = "Mortality rate"
    ),
    type = list(c(all_continuous(), Mortality) ~ "continuous2"),
    statistic = list(
      c(Male, Age, BMI, LOS) ~ c(
        "{mean} ({sd})",
        "{median} [{p25}, {p75}]",
        "{min} - {max}"
      ),
      c(
        `N sample`,
        `NACh(R)Th`,
        `Complications`,
        `Severe complications`,
        `Anastomotic leak`,
        Infection,
        Mortality
      ) ~ c("{median} [{p25}, {p75}]", "{min} - {max}"),
      N ~ c("{median} [{p25}, {p75}]", "{min} - {max}", "{sum}")
    ),
    missing_text = "Missing"
  ) |>
  modify_footnote("stat_0" ~ NA) |>
  modify_table_body(
    ~ .x |>
      mutate(
        label = case_when(
          row_type == "label" &
            var_type %in% c("categorical", "dichotomous") ~ paste0(label, "†"),
          row_type == "label" &
            var_type %in% c("continuous", "continuous2") ~ paste0(label, "*"),
          TRUE ~ label
        )
      )
  ) |>
  tab_tbl() |>
  align(j = 2, align = "center", part = "all")
```

Presentation of variables: \* -- Mean (SD) (optional), Median \[Q1, Q3\] and Min - Max; † -- absolute frequency (percent).

\
Most studies (88%) were published after 2009 and had a retrospective design (85%). Ileostomies were used in almost 60% of studies, ileostomy or colostomy in 40%, and colostomy alone in only 2.7%. Fifty percent of studies had a sample size within the interquartile range of 100 to 539, with a maximum of 17,867. Estimated pooled values were: mean male proportion 61%, mean age 62 years, mean BMI 24.7 kg/m², and mean LOS 11.2 days; median relative rates were NACh(R)Th 50%, overall complications 30%, severe complications 7.3%, anastomotic leak 5.6%, infection 10.9%, and mortality 0.3%. However, much of the data were unavailable across studies (cumulative absolute counts were not reported, not assessed, or only relative results were presented).

\
Figure 4. Forest plot for pooled incidence of anastomotic leak.
```{r}
#| label: 6-forest-al-overall
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 16

m.prop <- df |>
  filter_out(is.na(`Anastomotic leak`)) |>
  mutate(
    `Publication Year` = factor(
      ifelse(
        `Publication Year` < 2010,
        "<2010",
        ifelse(`Publication Year` >= 2020, "≥2020", "2010-2019")
      ),
      levels = c("<2010", "2010-2019", "≥2020")
    )
  ) |>
  metaprop(
    event = `Anastomotic leak`,
    n = N,
    studlab = Author_year,
    data = _,
    method = "GLMM",
    sm = "PLOGIT",
    common = F,
    random = T,
    prediction = T,
    method.random.ci = "HK",
    method.predict = "HTS"
  )

forest(
  m.prop,
  common = F,
  random = T,
  overall = T,
  prediction = T,
  pooled.totals = T,
  pooled.events = T,
  backtransf = T,
  print.I2.ci = T,
  print.tau2.ci = F,
  pscale = 100,
  xlim = c(0, 30),
  at = seq(0, 30, 5),
  smlab = "",
  xlab = "Anastomotic leak, %",
  leftcols = c("studlab", "n", "event"),
  leftlabs = c("Author, Year (subset)", "N sample", "Events"),
  rightcols = c("effect", "ci"),
  rightlabs = c("Proportion, %", "95% CI"),
  digits = 2,
  fontsize = 10,
  spacing = 1,
  col.square = "grey75",
  col.diamond.random = "blue",
  col.predict = "red"
)
```

Diamond -- pooled effect, vertical reference line -- pooled estimate.

Included: 67 studies, 26,534 patients, 2,391 events.

\
Statistical heterogeneity was high: I² = 85.3% (95% CI 82.1; 88.0), τ² = 0.3689 (p \< 0.0001). In the random-effects model, the pooled incidence of anastomotic leak was 7.04% (95% CI 6.00; 8.25), with a prediction interval of 2.18%; 20.50%. On average, the expected rate of anastomotic leak after TME with primary anastomosis and a defunctioning stoma is around 7%, but in a new study the observed rate could reasonably range from about 2% to 20%.

\
Figure 5. Forest plot for pooled incidence of anastomotic leak in subgroup analysis (type stoma).
```{r}
#| label: 7-forest-al-stoma
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 17

m.prop.sub.stoma <- update(
  m.prop,
  subgroup = Stomy,
  tau.common = F,
  prediction.subgroup = T,
  method.predict = "HTS",
  subset = Stomy != "colo"
)

pool_group <- !(m.prop.sub.stoma$subgroup.levels %in%
  c("colo"))

forest(
  m.prop.sub.stoma,
  common = F,
  random = T,
  overall = F,
  prediction = F,
  pooled.totals = T,
  pooled.events = T,
  backtransf = T,
  print.I2 = T,
  print.I2.ci = T,
  print.tau2.ci = F,
  overall.hetstat = F,
  subgroup = pool_group,
  subgroup.hetstat = pool_group,
  random.subgroup = pool_group,
  prediction.subgroup = pool_group,
  pscale = 100,
  xlim = c(0, 30),
  at = seq(0, 30, 5),
  smlab = "",
  xlab = "Anastomotic leak, %",
  leftcols = c("studlab", "n", "event"),
  leftlabs = c("Author, Year (subset)", "N sample", "Events"),
  rightcols = c("effect", "ci"),
  rightlabs = c("Proportion, %", "95% CI"),
  digits = 2,
  fontsize = 10,
  spacing = 1,
  col.square = "grey75",
  col.diamond.random = "blue",
  col.predict = "red"
)
```

Diamond -- pooled effect, vertical reference line -- pooled estimate.

Included: ileostomy, 39 studies, 17,740 patients, 1,699 events; ileostomy + colostomy, 26 studies, 8,516 patients, 679 events (colostomy alone, 2 studies, 278 patients, 13 events, was not pooled).

\
The colostomy subgroup was not analyzed separately, as it included only 2 studies. Heterogeneity remained high within each subgroup (I² = 84.1% and 87.3%). Pooled estimates and prediction intervals were similar between subgroups. The test for subgroup difference was not significant (p = 0.789).

```{r}
#| label: 8-reg-stoma
#| eval: false

reg.stomy <- df |>
  filter_out(is.na(`Anastomotic leak`)) |>
  filter(Stomy != "colo") |>
  rma.glmm(
    measure = "PLO",
    xi = `Anastomotic leak`,
    ni = N,
    mods = ~Stomy,
    data = _,
    method = "ML"
  ) |>
  broom::tidy(conf.int = T, exp = T) |>
  mutate(
    Parameter = c("Intercept", "Ileo-/colostomy"),
    `OR (95% CI)` = ifelse(
      Parameter == "Intercept",
      "1",
      paste0(
        round(estimate, 2),
        " (",
        round(conf.low, 2),
        "; ",
        round(conf.high, 2),
        ")"
      )
    ),
    `p-value` = ifelse(Parameter == "Intercept", "-", round(p.value, 3))
  ) |>
  select(Parameter:`p-value`)
```

Diamond -- pooled effect, vertical reference line -- pooled estimate.

Included: retrospective cohorts, 57 studies, 24,403 patients, 2,172 events; prospective cohorts, 6 studies, 1,520 patients, 186 events; RCTs, 4 studies, 611 patients, 33 events.

\
The analysis included 6 prospective and 4 randomized studies. Heterogeneity also remained fairly high. Due to the small number of studies, pooled estimates and prediction intervals were unstable, and the subgroup difference was not significant (p = 0.411); given the low power of this comparison, this should not be read as evidence that design does not affect the leak rate.

\
Heterogeneity was similarly high. Regardless of publication year, pooled estimates and prediction intervals were broadly similar, and the subgroup difference was not significant (p = 0.246).

```{r}
#| label: 12-reg-year
#| eval: false

df |>
  filter_out(is.na(`Anastomotic leak`)) |>
  mutate(
    `Publication Year` = factor(
      ifelse(
        `Publication Year` < 2010,
        "<2010",
        ifelse(`Publication Year` >= 2020, "≥2020", "2010-2019")
      ),
      levels = c("<2010", "2010-2019", "≥2020")
    )
  ) |>
  rma.glmm(
    measure = "PLO",
    xi = `Anastomotic leak`,
    ni = N,
    mods = ~`Publication Year`,
    data = _,
    method = "ML"
  ) |>
  broom::tidy(conf.int = T, exp = T) |>
  mutate(
    Parameter = c(
      "Intercept",
      "2010-2019 publication year",
      "≥2020 publication year"
    ),
    `OR (95% CI)` = ifelse(
      Parameter == "Intercept",
      "1",
      paste0(
        round(estimate, 2),
        " (",
        round(conf.low, 2),
        "; ",
        round(conf.high, 2),
        ")"
      )
    ),
    `p-value` = ifelse(Parameter == "Intercept", "-", round(p.value, 3))
  ) |>
  select(Parameter:`p-value`) |>
  tab_ME() |>
  align(j = 2:3, align = "center", part = "all")
```

Included: (a) and (c), 67 studies, 26,534 patients, 2,391 events; (b) studies with n ≥ 150, 26 studies, 22,700 patients, 2,057 events; (d) 92 studies (67 observed and 25 imputed).

```{r}
#| label: 16-funnel-metareg

m.metareg.logN <- df |>
  filter_out(is.na(`Anastomotic leak`)) |>
  mutate(logN = log10(N)) |>
  rma.glmm(
    measure = "PLO",
    xi = `Anastomotic leak`,
    ni = N,
    mods = ~logN,
    data = _,
    method = "ML",
    test = "t"
  )
```

\
On the logit scale, the funnel plot of all studies looks asymmetric (Figure 11a), with low-rate studies spread towards large standard errors. This is largely a property of the scale: the standard error of a logit-transformed proportion depends on the proportion itself, so studies with low event rates have larger standard errors regardless of their size. Accordingly, the funnel plot on the arcsine scale, where the standard error depends only on the sample size, is largely symmetric (Figure 11c). Peters' test, which does not share this dependency, was not significant (p `r p_peters_all <- metabias(m.prop, method.bias = "peters")$p.value; ifelse(p_peters_all < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste0("= ", round(p_peters_all, 3)))`), and neither was a meta-regression of the logit proportion on log~10~ sample size (OR per 10-fold increase in sample size `r round(exp(coef(m.metareg.logN)["logN"]), 2)`, 95% CI `r round(exp(m.metareg.logN$ci.lb[2]), 2)`; `r round(exp(m.metareg.logN$ci.ub[2]), 2)`, p = `r round(m.metareg.logN$pval[2], 3)`). The residual irregularity of the funnel is more plausibly explained by the high between-study heterogeneity than by small-study effects.

\
When the analysis was restricted to studies with a sample size of at least 150 (k = `r m.prop.sub150$k`; Figure 11b), Peters' test was significant (p `r p_peters_150 <- metabias(m.prop.sub150, method.bias = "peters")$p.value; ifelse(p_peters_150 < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste0("= ", round(p_peters_150, 3)))`). This is an isolated finding of a secondary analysis, sensitive to a few small studies with very high leak rates, and it was not supported by the other analyses; we therefore did not interpret it as evidence of publication bias.

\
As a sensitivity analysis, the Duval & Tweedie trim-and-fill method was applied to impute studies that would restore funnel-plot symmetry, providing an estimate of the pooled effect if the apparent funnel-plot asymmetry were driven by publication bias. Because this asymmetry was not confirmed by Peters' test or by the meta-regression, the trim-and-fill estimate should be read as a worst-case scenario rather than a corrected estimate. Figure 11d shows the effect that the imputed studies (n = 25) would need to have.

\
As part of the sensitivity analysis, we decided to supplement the GLMM results with those from the inverse-variance method and the Duval & Tweedie trim-and-fill method, to assess the robustness of the findings.

\
Table 2. Comparison of several methods for estimating the pooled effect.
```{r}
#| label: 17-method-comparison

m.prop.IV <- df |>
  filter_out(is.na(`Anastomotic leak`)) |>
  mutate(
    `Publication Year` = factor(
      ifelse(
        `Publication Year` < 2010,
        "<2010",
        ifelse(`Publication Year` >= 2020, "≥2020", "2010-2019")
      ),
      levels = c("<2010", "2010-2019", "≥2020")
    )
  ) |>
  metaprop(
    event = `Anastomotic leak`,
    n = N,
    studlab = Author_year,
    data = _,
    method = "Inverse",
    method.tau = "ML",
    sm = "PLOGIT",
    common = F,
    random = T,
    prediction = T,
    method.random.ci = "HK",
    method.predict = "HTS"
  )

to_percent <- function(x) 100 * plogis(x)

tibble(
  Model = c("GLMM", "IV", "Trim-and-fill method"),
  Estimate = c(
    to_percent(m.prop$TE.random),
    to_percent(m.prop.IV$TE.random),
    to_percent(m.prop.trim$TE.random)
  ),
  CI_lower = c(
    to_percent(m.prop$lower.random),
    to_percent(m.prop.IV$lower.random),
    to_percent(m.prop.trim$lower.random)
  ),
  CI_upper = c(
    to_percent(m.prop$upper.random),
    to_percent(m.prop.IV$upper.random),
    to_percent(m.prop.trim$upper.random)
  ),
  PI_lower = c(
    to_percent(m.prop$lower.predict),
    to_percent(m.prop.IV$lower.predict),
    to_percent(m.prop.trim$lower.predict)
  ),
  PI_upper = c(
    to_percent(m.prop$upper.predict),
    to_percent(m.prop.IV$upper.predict),
    to_percent(m.prop.trim$upper.predict)
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    `Pooled proportion\n(95% CI)` = sprintf(
      "%.2f%% (%.2f; %.2f)",
      Estimate,
      CI_lower,
      CI_upper
    ),
    `95% prediction interval` = sprintf("%.2f%%; %.2f%%", PI_lower, PI_upper)
  ) |>
  select(Model, `Pooled proportion\n(95% CI)`, `95% prediction interval`) |>
  tab_ME() |>
  align(j = 2:3, align = "center", part = "all")
```

GLMM -- generalized linear mixed-effects model, IV -- inverse-variance, Trim-and-fill method -- Duval & Tweedie trim and fill method.

Included: GLMM and IV, 67 studies, 26,534 patients, 2,391 events; trim-and-fill, 92 studies (67 observed and 25 imputed).

\
Results of the GLMM and IV methods are similar (7.04% and 7.45%). However, the estimate recovered by the Duval & Tweedie trim-and-fill method was higher (10.49%, 95% CI 8.75; 12.52) and had a wider prediction interval (2.18%; 38.09%), suggesting that the risk of anastomotic leak could be higher if the asymmetry reflected publication bias, a scenario that was not supported by the other analyses.

Figure 8-9. Forest plots for pooled incidence of (a) all postoperative complications and (b) severe postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo Grade 3-5).
```{r}
#| label: 23-forest-compl-combined
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 14.5

# meta::forest() draws with grid on its own device, so each plot is rendered
# to PNG and then stacked with patchwork
forest_png <- function(m, xlim, at, xlab, height, dpi = 300) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  ragg::agg_png(f, width = 9, height = height, units = "in", res = dpi)
  forest(
    m,
    common = F,
    random = T,
    overall = T,
    prediction = T,
    pooled.totals = T,
    pooled.events = T,
    backtransf = T,
    print.I2.ci = T,
    print.tau2.ci = F,
    pscale = 100,
    xlim = xlim,
    at = at,
    smlab = "",
    xlab = xlab,
    leftcols = c("studlab", "n", "event"),
    leftlabs = c("Author, Year (subset)", "N sample", "Events"),
    rightcols = c("effect", "ci"),
    rightlabs = c("Proportion, %", "95% CI"),
    digits = 2,
    fontsize = 10,
    spacing = 1,
    col.square = "grey75",
    col.diamond.random = "blue",
    col.predict = "red"
  )
  dev.off()
  wrap_elements(full = grid::rasterGrob(png::readPNG(f), interpolate = TRUE))
}

forest_png(m.prop.compl, c(0, 100), seq(0, 100, 10), "30-day morbidity, %", 8) /
  forest_png(
    m.prop.compl.sev,
    c(0, 50),
    seq(0, 50, 10),
    "Severe complications, %",
    6.5
  ) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(8, 6.5)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16))
```

Diamond -- pooled effect, vertical reference line -- pooled estimate.

Table 6. Total number of stoma-related complications by type and studies reporting them.
```{r}
#| label: 24-stoma-compl-total

df |>
  pivot_longer(
    `Стома-ассоциированные ранние осложнения`:`Парастомальная грыжа`
  ) |>
  filter_out(is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(
    name = unname(stoma_compl_en[name]),
    Author_year = str_squish(Author_year)
  ) |>
  summarise(
    Total = sum(value),
    Studies = paste0(Author_year, " (", value, ")", collapse = "; "),
    .by = name
  ) |>
  # The aggregate "Stoma-related early complications" is the overall total and goes last
  mutate(is_total = name == "Stoma-related early complications") |>
  arrange(is_total, desc(Total), name) |>
  mutate(
    name = ifelse(is_total, "Total (all stoma-related complications)", name)
  ) |>
  select(
    `Stoma morbidity` = name,
    `Total events` = Total,
    `Studies (events)` = Studies
  ) |>
  tab_ME() |>
  bold(i = ~ startsWith(`Stoma morbidity`, "Total"), part = "body") |>
  align(j = 2, align = "center", part = "all")
```
